analysis.title: Paul Donovan's daily audio: Defiant consumers?
key_insights: Friday's crypto and technology moves are described as attention grabbing but economically muted. The crypto moves are called speculation with little real-world relevance, and the technology moves reflect concerns in one sector rather than a general economic crisis.
US consumer behavior has followed a pattern broadly similar to that of other consumers less exposed to technology equities.
German September retail sales initial releases carry a strong pessimism bias, with revisions showing consumers shopping more. The unreliable initial figures may explain modest market interest.

The week has a clutter of business sentiment polls. The price sub-components of the US ISM poll may get extra attention because of investor focus on pricing power, but UBS says to treat them with caution since factory gate prices are far removed from consumer pricing.

Investors assume Washington gridlock after the US midterm elections, which is not much change from today. The focus is whether President Trump becomes more aggressive in the Gulf war once he is freed from the pursuit of popularity.

sector_views.rationale: Friday's technology moves reflected concerns in one sector and did not signal a general economic crisis.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Initial releases carry a pessimism bias and are later revised to show stronger consumer spending, so the first print draws only modest market interest.
Could get extra attention given investor focus on pricing power, but factory gate prices are far removed from consumer prices, so the signal should be treated with caution.

crypto_views: Crypto moves on Friday are described as speculation with little real-world relevance, apart from the alleged boost to North Korea's GDP.
risk_factors: Trump becoming more aggressive in the Gulf war after the midterm elections.
